text: Given 5 technicians in `technicians`, each starting at 0 matching tickets for the given status/queueIDs, when 10 tickets are assigned concurrently via autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource, then every technician ends up with exactly 2 tickets (max-min spread across technicians <= 1)
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). This test asserts spread === [2,2,2,2,2] across 5 technicians after 10 concurrent createTicket calls, and that every created ticket queueID matches the single queueIDs entry given. Code review follow-up (Kaka Zhang, 2026-10-21): this test originally passed for the wrong reason -- STATUS was 1, which happened to equal the mock create-ticket routes bare default status, masking that the tool never set a created tickets own status. STATUS is now 8 (deliberately distinct from that default); this test only stays green because tool.handler.ts now defaults payload.status to the filter value on createTicket (see TC-DEV2).
note: r2: re-implemented against the new technicians/status/queueIDs contract (requirement change, see PRD-20620-r2.md Rework triage) -- same AC as round 1's TC1, different input shape.

text: Given two calls share the same status/queueIDs/technicians combination and are issued so their counting steps would overlap without serialization, when both complete, then the second call's decision reflects the first call's result, not a stale snapshot -- the two calls never both pick the same technician off the same stale count
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). Gates call As Tickets/query to force a controlled overlap window with call B issued synchronously before any await; asserts B genuinely waits and then picks the other resource. Code review follow-up (Kaka Zhang, 2026-10-21): also exposed by the STATUS=8 change above (same masking as TC1 -- the created tickets own status is what makes the second calls count see the first calls write at all); passes now via the same createTicket default-status fix (TC-DEV2).

text: Given a live Autotask sandbox/INT environment with a real technicians list, when 5 test-prefixed tickets are created/reassigned through autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource with a real status/queueIDs filter, then the Autotask UI shows assignees spread per the least-matching-count rule and each assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID matches what the tool reported
steps: In INT/staging with real Autotask credentials, pick 3 or more real technicians (resourceID + roleID) and a real status/queueIDs combination
Call autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource 5 times with a clearly test-prefixed ticket title, passing the same technicians/status/queueIDs each time
Open the queue(s) in the Autotask UI and record each ticket's assignee and role
Compare against the tool's reported assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID for each call
expect: Assignees are spread (no single technician holds more than ceil(5/3)=2 of the 5 tickets) and the UI's assignee/role matches the tool's reported assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID for every ticket

text: MUST FIX (Kaka Zhang code review, 2026-10-21): given a createTicket call under a status filter that does not coincide with Autotasks own default status for a new ticket, when the tool creates the ticket, then it must set the new tickets own status to the filter value (unless the caller explicitly named a status in createTicket) so the NEXT call under the same filter actually counts it -- without this, a technician looks permanently unloaded under any status filter that is not the create-time default.
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). Two sequential (non-concurrent) createTicket calls for the same technicians/status/queueIDs: first lands on the lower-id technician, second must land on the other one; verified against a source revert this test fails (both land on the same technician) without the fix -- see PRD-20620 self-test note on red-before-fix verification.

text: MUST FIX, remaining gap: given the caller explicitly sets createTicket.status to a value different from the counting filter (a real shape -- workflow rules transition status asynchronously), when a second call arrives under the same filter before Autotasks own data reflects the first assignment, then the tool must still not repeat the same technician -- covered by an in-process reservation (assignment-reservations.ts), not by live Autotask data. Also verifies the reservation expires (TTL) rather than padding forever.
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). Caller sets createTicket.status=1 while filtering status=8; tool leaves the created tickets real status at 1 (does not override explicit caller intent) but the second call still picks the other technician via the reservation; after advancing fake timers past the 2-minute TTL, a third call reverts to the lowest-id technician, proving the padding expires rather than accumulating.

text: Given two calls share a status and at least one technician but are not identical sets (e.g. [A,B] and [A,B,C]), when both are issued so their counting steps would overlap, then they must still serialize on the shared technician(s) -- the original single combined-key lock missed this because the two calls composite keys differ.
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). Gates the first calls Tickets/query; the second call ([A,B,C]) issued synchronously must not write until the first ([A,B]) releases; asserts [A,B] picks A, [A,B,C] then picks B (never A again).

text: Given an existing ticket being reassigned is itself one of its current assignees matching tickets, when counting that assignees load for the pick, then the ticket being moved must be excluded from their count (it is about to leave them) -- otherwise a tie-break can pile a second matching ticket onto the wrong technician.
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 14 passed, 14 total (exit 0). TECH_HIGHs only matching ticket is the one being reassigned (ticketID=5001); TECH_LOW has one unrelated matching ticket. Without exclusion both read count=1 and the lowest-id tie-break picks TECH_LOW; asserts the tool instead reports TECH_HIGH=0 (excluded), TECH_LOW=1, and assigns to TECH_HIGH.
